title: Pipeline Ledger
description: D-83. The lifecycle store for ideas that have NOT fired yet. Distinct from contracts/ledger.schema.json (the Nomination Ledger), which tracks the d1..d15 OUTCOME of names already nominated. This store answers a different question: what did the committee think was worth keeping alive, and what has to happen for it to come back? Only names the committee itself proposed (committee.schema.json ledger_proposal) land here — post-market files, it never judges. Sole writer: tools/pipeline_ledger.py.

origin_date.description: the session date whose committee proposed it

origin_session.description: which pass produced it, e.g. premarket_committee / intraday_pod

origin_verdict.description: the committee verdict it carried that day (PASS / HOLD-FOR-CONDITIONS) — context for why it is here and not in the plan

case_snapshot.description: the committee's own reason, verbatim. This is what gets read back when the name re-surfaces — it is why a re-surface never needs a re-nomination.

classification.description: daily_reconsider = re-fed into every morning's tally, re-scored fresh. trigger_silent = parked and silent until `trigger` fires.

trigger.description: NON-NULL and required when classification is trigger_silent (the tool rejects the row otherwise). `field` is a dotted path into the AQE export record, e.g. sc_momentum or bracket.entry.

status.description: active = being watched. fired = its trigger hit (market-hours/premarket sweep surfaces it). expired = TTL ran out with nothing happening. closed = resolved deliberately (it advanced into the plan, or the PM dropped it).

expiry_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Bounded TTL — an idea dies stale unless re-proposed. Re-proposal by a later committee extends it.

last_seen.description: last date a sweep touched this row

fired_note.description: the actual observed value that satisfied the trigger — the anchor, not just 'it fired'

proposed_count.description: how many separate sessions have proposed this name — a repeatedly-proposed setup that never fires is itself a signal

history.description: append-only audit trail of every state change (law 3: bounded and logged, never silently mutated)
